story.title: Story 6: Legacy File-Store Retirement And Compatibility Cleanup

result.planSummary: Hardened lh-context inspection so mixed legacy-JSON plus SQLite thread directories now prefer SQLite as authoritative, surface the selected backing in inspection/report outputs, and warn operators how to clean up split-brain risk; added Story 6 regressions for dual-source inspection and a source-truth grep guard over active runtime/maintenance/compact paths.

changedFiles.reason: Changed inspection loading to prefer SQLite in auto mode when both backings exist, avoid silent fallback to legacy JSON, and emit explicit dual-source cleanup warnings.
Surfaced the selected backing on summary, tokens, bands, and readiness inspection results.
Propagated backing metadata into post-compact report output.
Added backing lines to human-readable lh-context inspection/report output so operators can see source truth directly.
Extended public inspection/report result types with backing metadata.
Updated formatter fixtures for the new backing field.
Added Story 6 regression coverage proving inspection prefers SQLite and warns explicitly when stale legacy JSON shadows a live managed thread.
Added the root smoke/grep guard that blocks legacy managed JSON references in active runtime, maintenance, and compact entry paths.

findingsFixed: Inspection no longer silently trusts legacy thread JSON when a live thread directory also contains thread.sqlite; auto mode now treats SQLite as authoritative and warns with cleanup guidance.
Inspection/report payloads and human output now identify the selected backing explicitly so rollback/source-truth state is inspectable by operators.
Added executable guardrails for Story 6 by covering dual-source inspection behavior and asserting active runtime/maintenance/compact files do not hard-code legacy managed JSON sources.

result.recommendedNextStep: Hand this to verification for Story 6 acceptance, with focus on AC-7.4/7.5 evidence from the new dual-source inspection regression and the active-path legacy-source guard.
